newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Peters says no plans for NZ capital gains tax.
newsitem.headline: Peters says no plans for NZ capital gains tax.

text.p: New Zealand Treasurer Winston Peters said on Wednesday that the government had no plans to introduce a capital gains tax.
Peters issued a statement after Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash said the absence of CGT was an anomaly in the New Zealand tax structure.
Committee chairman Tony Ryall said taxes on capital gains were "full of loopholes" and the government wanted to reduce taxes, not increase them.
He said the impact on the real productive economy would be bad for jobs and growth.
Labour Minister Max Bradford said such taxes had not stopped property speculation in other countries and would not do so in New Zealand.
